item.title: 'Never felt better': Donald Trump shuts down health rumours? Asks 'are you better off?'
item.description: Amidst online speculation about his health, Donald Trump declared on Truth Social that he has "never felt better." Following this statement, the former US president quickly shifted focus to politics, asserting that Washington, D.C., is now a "crime-free zone." He also shared a post highlighting America's supposed thriving state under his leadership.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘We haven't taken anything off the table’: Kristi Noem signals expanding ICE ops; Chicago next in line after Los Angeles
item.description: The Trump administration plans to broaden immigration enforcement across US cities. Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem confirms ongoing ICE operations, with intentions to increase resources. Focus is on cities with sanctuary policies and high crime rates. Governor JB Pritzker criticizes the approach as dangerous. Noem encourages cooperation from cities, emphasizing safety. The administration denies political bias in enforcement decisions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 6.0 magnitude earthquake hits Afghanistan: Two children killed in roof collapse; tremors felt in Pakistan
item.description: A 6.0 magnitude earthquake struck eastern Afghanistan late Sunday. The quake's epicenter was near Jalalabad. Tragically, two children died and several others were injured. The tremors were felt across eastern Afghanistan and in Islamabad, Pakistan. Afghanistan is prone to earthquakes. This disaster follows recent flooding in Nangarhar province, which caused further devastation. The region faces ongoing challenges.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Rudy Giuliani injured in New Hampshire car crash: Hospitalized with fractured vertebrae; spokesman says Ex-NYC mayor in ‘good spirits’
item.description: Rudy Giuliani, 81, was hospitalized in New Hampshire after a high-speed car accident on Saturday night. He sustained a fractured vertebrae and other injuries after being struck from behind. Prior to the accident, Giuliani had assisted a woman who was a victim of domestic violence, contacting 911 and remaining on the scene until police arrived.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Huthis raid UN premises in Yemen: At least 11 aid workers detained; crackdown follows Israeli strike
item.description: United Nations reports the detention of its staff by Huthi rebels in Yemen. The detentions occurred after an Israeli strike. Hans Grundberg, the UN envoy, condemned these actions. He demanded immediate release of the personnel. The World Food Programme also confirmed a staff member's detention. The Huthis accused aid workers of spying.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Our country would be completely destroyed': Trump defends tariffs after US court setback; thanks Obama-appointed judge
item.description: Donald Trump defended his trade policy after a court declared most of his tariffs illegal. He thanked a judge who sided with him. Trump claimed tariffs brought trillions of dollars to the US. A court ruled Trump overstepped his authority with the tariffs. The levies were set to cover about 69 percent of US imports.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Steel, de minimis & China: Court declares ‘most’ Trump tariffs illegal - what levies are spared
item.description: A US court has deemed most of Donald Trump's reciprocal tariffs illegal. However, sector-specific tariffs like those on steel and aluminum remain. These tariffs are central to Trump's trade strategy. Tariffs on Chinese imports, maintained by Joe Biden, are also unaffected. The elimination of the 'de minimis' exemption impacts small businesses. The administration may appeal to the Supreme Court.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Skimpy process, startling argument’: Judge halts Trump’s mass deportation push - what she said
item.description: A US judge has stopped the Trump administration's plan. The plan aimed to quickly deport more undocumented migrants. Judge Jia Cobb cited concerns about due process. The ruling blocks the expansion of expedited removal. This process allows deportation without a court hearing. Donald Trump wanted to deport one million people yearly. Critics worry about people not knowing their rights.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Jakarta protests: President Prabowo cancels foreign visit; fires, deaths reported across Indonesia
item.description: President Prabowo Subianto canceled his China visit due to escalating unrest across Indonesia, sparked by protests over lawmaker pay and a fatal traffic incident. Demonstrations intensified, resulting in parliament buildings being torched in several regions and casualties reported in Makassar. The government is now addressing the crisis by summoning social media companies to moderate content and combat disinformation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Disney World: ‘White powder alert’ to ‘protein spill’; here are what the park's secret codes mean
item.description: Disney World employees use secret code words to handle incidents discreetly, revealed in a Reddit thread. Codes like 'white powder alert' for ash scattering and 'protein spill' for vomit are used to avoid panic. Former employees also shared challenges, including low pay, demanding work, and strict rules regarding technology use backstage.

item.title: Alaska bear attack: Woman mauled and dragged 100 yards; family raises $63,700 for care
item.description: Ariean Fabrizio Colton, a nurse in Kenai, Alaska, survived a brutal brown bear attack during her morning jog. The bear ambushed and dragged her over 100 yards, leaving her with severe facial and scalp injuries. She was airlifted to Anchorage for surgery and faces a long recovery, while officials urge caution due to increased bear activity.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: MAGA podcaster in spotlight: From plagiarism scandals to DC press seat; who is Benny Johnson?
item.description: Benny Johnson, a conservative commentator with a history of controversies, was invited to a White House press briefing, where he made unsubstantiated claims about crime in Washington, D.C. Despite discrepancies in his account, the administration praised his comments, signalling a preference for right-leaning influencers over traditional media. Johnson's prominent role highlights the increasing reliance on figures known for spreading misinformation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘We caught them, cold’: Donald Trump blasts workers for Rose Garden damage; shares video
item.description: Donald Trump publicly criticised a subcontractor for damaging the newly renovated White House Rose Garden, sharing security footage of the incident on Truth Social. Trump described a significant gash in the limestone, blaming the damage on workers using a faulty cart.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Where is Jonathan Hoang? Loved ones march for missing autistic Arlington man; family believes he was kidnapped
item.description: Family and friends of Jonathan Hoang, missing for five months, marched in Kirkland ahead of his 22nd birthday on August 30th. Jonathan, who has autism, disappeared on March 30th, and his family suspects he was kidnapped. A $100,000 reward is offered for information.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: WH visit denied: Dyan Cannon faces Secret Service roadblock over passport- Who is this actress
item.description: Dyan Cannon, 88, faced an unexpected White House lockout due to a discrepancy in her passport age. Accompanied by fellow actresses and a chef for their podcast, 'God's Table,' Cannon's past age fib caused a delay. Despite the hiccup, Cannon humorously embraced the situation, reaffirming that age is just a number.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: So what I took the hat, life is first come...: Rich Polish CEO now threatens online trolls
item.description: Millionaire CEO Piotr Szczerek, infamous for snatching a signed hat from a child at the US Open, allegedly defended his actions in a statement, claiming "first come, first served." He also threatened legal action against online critics. "I understand that some people might not like it, but please, let's not make a global scandal out of the hat. It's just a hat. If yoy were faster, you would have it," he reportedly said on a Goworkd forum.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
